questions.q: Why is Welch's method better than a single FFT of the whole log?
options: It needs no scipy and runs on numpy
questions.explain: Averaging overlapping windows gives a stable spectrum estimate at a chosen resolution; a single FFT is noisy and depends on the recording length.

questions.q: Spectral resolution at fs = 8000 Hz and nperseg = 1024:

options: Gyro rebound after the stick stops
Setpoint overshoot when entering a maneuver

questions.q: What do you use to read an ArduPilot .bin in Python?
Which part of the flight do you use for a Welch spectrum?
options: Any segment at least 5 seconds long
questions.explain: A stationary segment; otherwise the peaks smear.

questions.q: What does a std of log row intervals > 10 µs at 8 kHz indicate?
options: A bad SD card that writes with a delay
questions.explain: A mean of 125 µs with a scatter of a few µs is normal.

questions.q: One way to determine the lag between setpoint and gyro is:
options: From the difference of the mean values
From the time of the first gyro peak
From the peak frequency in the spectrum
questions.explain: The shift at which the setpoint–gyro correlation is greatest; `step_metrics` uses the simpler 50 %-crossing difference.

questions.q: What does a spectrogram show that a single spectrum does not?
options: Only the amplitude at one frequency
How noise frequencies change over time and with throttle
questions.explain: A spectrogram is a spectrum over windows in time: you can see the motor harmonics crawl with throttle.
